metadata.notes: Some training entries may contain transcription errors introduced during digitization. Cross-validate all entries against derived rules before use.

discovered_properties.notes: Uses named tokens for digit values and power values. When a smaller-valued token immediately precedes a larger-valued token, the values multiply. When a larger-valued token precedes a smaller one (or equal-valued tokens appear), the values add. Powers appear in descending order in canonical forms. An implicit multiplier of 1 applies when a power token has no preceding digit token.
discovered_properties.canonical_form: Largest power first, each power preceded by its multiplier (omitted if 1), remainder digit appended at end
open_questions: Confirm exact base value from training distribution
Verify no morphophonological alternations at morpheme boundaries

token_analysis.method: Query the morphemes table for surface forms, values, and categories

digits.query: SELECT surface_form, value FROM morphemes WHERE language='turahi' AND category='digit' ORDER BY value

powers.query: SELECT surface_form, value FROM morphemes WHERE language='turahi' AND category='power' ORDER BY value
powers.progression_hint: Each power is the previous power times the base

discovered_properties.notes: Uses pivot (delimiter) words that separate multiplier groups from additive remainders. The system has a primary base and a sub-base for composing coefficient and remainder values. Tokens before a pivot word form a coefficient that multiplies the pivot value. Tokens after the last pivot form an additive remainder. Sub-base tokens compose additively within coefficient and remainder groups.
discovered_properties.canonical_form: Highest pivot first, coefficient before each pivot (omitted if 1), lowest-order remainder at end. Coefficients and remainders are composed using sub-base tokens in descending order.

structure.pivot_hierarchy: The system uses two pivot levels; the higher pivot equals the square of the lower pivot's value
structure.coefficient_composition: Coefficients use the sub-base tokens additively (e.g., sub-base-2 + digit-3 = sub-base value + 3)
structure.remainder_composition: Same additive sub-base composition as coefficients

open_questions: Determine primary base and sub-base values from morpheme table
Clarify exact pivot hierarchy and values

token_analysis.method: Query morphemes table; note the category distinctions

unit_digits.query: SELECT surface_form, value FROM morphemes WHERE language='belago' AND category='digit' ORDER BY value

sub_base_tokens.query: SELECT surface_form, value FROM morphemes WHERE language='belago' AND category='subbase' ORDER BY value
sub_base_tokens.note: These compose additively with digits to form coefficient values

pivot_tokens.query: SELECT surface_form, value FROM morphemes WHERE language='belago' AND category='power' ORDER BY value

discovered_properties.notes: Combines a multiplicative-additive composition rule (identical to Turahi's rule: smaller-before-larger multiplies, larger-before-smaller adds) with a subtractive morphological mechanism for expressing certain digit values. A specific morphological prefix applied to basic digit words derives values that represent complements from the base. For example, if the base is B and a digit d has value V, then prefix+d has value B-V.
discovered_properties.canonical_form: Same descending-power layout as Turahi. Subtractive digit forms are used for values from ceil(base/2)+1 through base-1.

subtractive_mechanism.prefix: Discoverable from the morphemes table — look for the 'subtractive' category entries and compare with basic digit forms to identify the shared prefix

open_questions: Identify the exact subtractive prefix morpheme
Determine the complement computation rule from attested forms
Map all subtractive digit forms to their computed values

token_analysis.method: Query morphemes table; note both 'digit' and 'subtractive' categories

basic_digits.query: SELECT surface_form, value FROM morphemes WHERE language='renshi' AND category='digit' ORDER BY value

derived_digits.query: SELECT surface_form, value FROM morphemes WHERE language='renshi' AND category='subtractive' ORDER BY value
derived_digits.note: Compare surface forms with basic digits to discover the derivation pattern

powers.query: SELECT surface_form, value FROM morphemes WHERE language='renshi' AND category='power' ORDER BY value

transcription_errors.description: During digitization of handwritten field notes, some training entries were incorrectly transcribed. The corrupted entries contain word forms that do not correctly encode their associated number values.
transcription_errors.estimated_rate: approximately 5-10% of training entries may be affected
error_types: morpheme substitution (wrong digit or power word used)
morpheme transposition (correct morphemes in wrong order)
morpheme insertion or deletion (extra or missing morphemes)
transcription_errors.detection_method: For each training entry, independently decode the word_form using the discovered composition rules and morpheme values, then compare the decoded value against the listed number. Any mismatch indicates a corrupted entry.

known_issues.confidence_field: The confidence field reflects the collector's subjective assessment at recording time and does NOT reliably indicate transcription errors introduced later during digitization. Do not use confidence alone to identify corrupted entries.

step_1_extract.description: Extract morpheme inventories from the database for each language using the queries specified in each language's token_analysis section

step_2_derive_rules.description: Using the morpheme inventories and the composition rules described above, build decode (word->number) and encode (number->word) functions for each language

step_3_validate.description: Cross-validate every training entry against the derived rules to identify corrupted entries
step_3_validate.output: List of corrupted entry IDs with corrections

step_4_process_tests.description: Process test cases from the test_decode, test_encode, and test_cross database tables

tables.test_decode: SELECT id, language, word_form FROM test_decode ORDER BY id
tables.test_encode: SELECT id, language, number FROM test_encode ORDER BY id
tables.test_cross: SELECT id, source_language, source_word, target_language FROM test_cross ORDER BY id

errors.json.description: JSON array of detected corrupted training entries, sorted by id

properties.id: integer — the training table row ID
properties.number: integer — the number value from the training entry
properties.wrong_word: string — the corrupted word_form currently in the database
properties.correct_word: string — the correct canonical word_form for this number

fix.sql.description: SQL UPDATE statements to correct each corrupted entry in the training table
fix.sql.format: One UPDATE statement per line: UPDATE training SET word_form = '<correct>' WHERE id = <id>;

decode_results.tsv.description: Tab-separated decode results, one row per test_decode entry

encode_results.tsv.description: Tab-separated encode results, one row per test_encode entry

cross_results.tsv.description: Tab-separated cross-system translation results, one row per test_cross entry
